claim: subject sways like a pendulum reacting to scroll motion

q1_defects.answer: No defects. Card hangs from a brass pivot rod with a bead at top-centre; everything sharp at DPR-2; full card chrome intact.

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads literally as a pendulum: the card is suspended from a thin brass rod/pin at top-centre and the body swings beneath it — idle hangs near-level, play-3 has swung clockwise to a clear ~15-20 deg tilt. Card chrome (brass header, 3 grey rows, ice dot, rounded panel) preserved, matches ground truth.

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes for 3 of 4. swayGain clearly scales swing amplitude (low near-level, high large swing); pivotLength clearly lengthens the suspension rod and drops/widens the swing; damping changes the settle. ambientSway is the exception — low and high are visually indistinguishable.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive: card swings across play frames, frameDeltaMag 5.82 then 6.27; controls apply ~571-592ms.

q5_net.answer: PLEASED — the hanging-pendulum metaphor is unmistakable and premium, the card stays fully legible, and 3 of 4 knobs are obvious. One nearly-dead knob is a taste flag, not a blocker.

flags.note: ambientSway control produces no user-legible change: low vs high are essentially the same frame (effRGB 70.4,65.8,59.8 both; meanAbsDiff 2.1). It is 1 of 4 controls so it does not cross the >1-dead-control MUST-FIX threshold, but a user would not notice it doing anything.
flags.evidence: control: ambientSway changedFrac 0.0528 meanAbsDiff 2.1, effRGB identical low/high
